Oh man I have never really missed a game like this one. I terribly regret not playing it more when I had the chance but I thought it was doing well and wasn't truly going to go away. I really do hope someone else picks this game up or makes a private server. I never really did like battle royale games but this one is fun. I was an 80s kid so it made it even more exciting. It even introduced me to a new band that plays in the intro video, Crazy Lixx.  

As for the gameplay, just think of any 80s action movie and mix it with a Red Dawn style BR game. Nothing like blazing across 80s brightly colored suburbia with submachine guns and rifles on a bicycle and a bandana with cutoff sleeve jackets and mullets with giant shades. Loved all the collectable mini games within the BR game and how different they all were. Like mini contestant shows while trying to survive. I just wish they could have survived long enough to add 80s action movie vehicles.

It's definitely got a lot of jank, but it's early access after all and that's honestly part of the charm with these types of games. It's pretty stable, matchmaking times are quick, they've been fixing bugs quickly, and it's certainly not anywhere near unplayable as some reviews have suggested.

The core gameplay of spawning in, collecting stuff, killing dudes and surviving is definitely solid and very addictive. The setting is ripe for the picking when it comes to adding fun and campy new settings, weapons, mechanics, and vehicles. Because it's not restricted by needing to be realistic, it's styled after an 80's gameshow afterall (think Running Man, SmashTV, etc.), the possibilities for new gameplay are only going to be restricted by the developer's imaginations.

Radical Heights is legitimately fun and it's easy to find yourself requieing for match after match, even after a crushing defeat, winning is definitely not a prerequisite for enjoying the game! I see lots of potential for the game to grow and improve in fun and interesting new ways. Hope that they find the support they need to continue developing it into the future.
